themes_detail.label: Sanitation Worker Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about sanitation workers or their vehicles spiked to 6 THIS WEEK, a 500% increase from the 1.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting possible service disruptions, vehicle condition issues, or worker conduct problems in CD 411.
evidence: 6 sanitation worker/vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.77)
500% spike from 8-week average, statistically significant deviation
Aligns with repeated CB budget requests for sanitation infrastructure upgrades, suggesting underlying systemic issues
reporting_angles: Interview residents about what specifically prompted complaints (missed pickups, damaged property, worker behavior)
Contact DSNY about staffing, vehicle maintenance, or route changes affecting CD 411 this week

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Spike
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK, a 380% increase over the 0.6 weekly average, marking an emerging pest control crisis that may indicate structural or sanitation vulnerabilities across the district.
evidence: 3 rodent complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 4.91)
Concurrent with sanitation and dumpster complaints, suggesting potential waste management failures
reporting_angles: Document locations of rodent sightings and interview affected residents about frequency and severity
Ask DSNY and Department of Health about seasonal trends or any known infestations in the area

themes_detail.label: Mold Outbreak Investigation
themes_detail.summary: Mold complaints surged to 6 two weeks ago (a 4700% spike from 0.1 weekly average), representing the most statistically extreme anomaly in the dataset; unclear if this reflects a weather-driven event, building defect pattern, or data artifact requiring immediate verification.
evidence: 6 mold complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 17.76, highest anomaly in dataset)
4700% increase—by far the most extreme spike in any complaint category
No follow-up complaints in most recent week, suggesting either resolution or reporting lag
reporting_angles: Determine if complaints cluster geographically (single building outbreak vs. district-wide issue)
Interview DOB and Health Department about whether mold complaints were linked to water intrusion, HVAC failures, or building violations

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints peaked at 11 two weeks ago, a 780% spike from the 1.2 weekly average, suggesting organized tree removal, construction damage, or a specific development project triggering violations across CD 411.
evidence: 11 illegal tree damage complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.2 weekly average (z-score: 8.95)
Multiple active ULURPs and 70 new building permits filed in past 90 days; development activity may be driving violations
reporting_angles: Cross-reference complaint locations with active development sites and ULURP applications (Northern Boulevard, 24th Avenue rezoning)
Contact Parks Enforcement Patrol about whether complaints are concentrated around construction zones or scattered across district

themes_detail.label: Homeless Assistance Requests Spike
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints jumped to 5 two weeks ago, a 700% increase from the 0.6 weekly average, indicating either a sudden surge in homelessness or heightened community awareness of encampments in this typically lower-density, residential district.
evidence: 5 homeless assistance complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 4.41)
CB budget requests include senior center and park improvements, suggesting aging infrastructure and limited social services
reporting_angles: Map 311 complaint locations to identify encampment hotspots; interview residents about visibility and duration of homeless presence
Contact NYC Department of Homeless Services about outreach efforts and shelter capacity in CD 411; explore whether recent policy changes or cold weather drove the spike
